cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella's back in its stand. Remember how I taught you to check your things before work? Handle's clean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is the canopy wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've moved beyond the handle. I gave it a rinse; let me dry it properly for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very thorough, at last. Have breakfast while I finish cleaning it. You can inspect the spokes again when it's back where it belongs.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 inspection lesson normalizes return; A3 grades B2 wet canopy as progress and offers drying; A5 credits B4 debris detection then schedules reinspection after it restores the item.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unexplained wetness gives A3 rinse story; B4 pondweed makes A5 further cleaning and a delayed inspection.

relationship.evidence: B4 naturally notices material evidence that the rinse story does not explain.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 thoroughness as a reason to take the object back for more work without revealing use.

specificity.evidence: A1 stand/work and B2 no rain establish suspicious restoration; B4 pondweed specifies hidden misuse.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 breakfast/reinspection request is practical control of the restoration, with no detached explanation of the concealment.
